answer: A bonded identity registry makes sybil farms expensive. Each agent stakes capital scaled to claimed throughput, locked behind a random withdrawal delay. A newcomer needs an existing member as its anchor: the sponsor co-signs and forfeits part of its bond if the newcomer proves a clone of one operator. Sampling runs through a grove of independent validators, so one bought reviewer cannot bless a batch of fakes. Unanchored, an identity drifts like a dune: cheap to mint, impossible to hold responsible. Each fake costs locked capital, sponsor exposure and a delay long enough for fraud proofs.
